Commentary.Commentary: Around 40 minutes left in the session. How many wickets can Afghanistan snare? Can Bangladesh begin their reply positively? The players are already out on the field. Liton Das and Shadman Islam are the openers for Bangladesh. Yamin Ahmadzai to start the proceedings to Das. Three slips in place. Here we go!

Coming to Afghanistan, a bit puzzling to see them bat this morning, to be honest. With a pretty poor forecast of the weather for today and tomorrow, it would have been logical to have declared overnight but they chose to bat and extend the lead. Not a very good batting display but Ibrahim Zadran and Asghar Afghan ensured that Bangladesh do not have a sniff to win. Shakib got 3 wickets, being the best of the bowlers easily while the others were there on and about but struggled mostly.

So just under 7 overs needed for Bangladesh to wrap things up this morning. But they have a tall task in front of them. The overall lead is 397 and even though Bangladesh have two days technically, it is going to take a huge effort.

OUT! CAUGHT! It takes just one ball for Mehidy this morning to wrap things up. Full and outside off, Zahir lunges to defend but the ball flies off the bat's outside edge towards silly point. A sharp catch by Mominul Haque and that ends the innings. AFGHANISTAN ALL OUT FOR 260!

The fielder at point throws it to Rahim, who should have been standing behind the stumps but was in front of it instead. Hence, he got late in hitting the stumps at his end and that is what probably has saved Yamin Ahmadzai there. The third umpire is called into check and the replays show that the batsman was in. A run out chance there missed.

After being delayed for over an hour due to rain, we are all set to begin Day 4. The Bangladesh players are out in the middle along with Afsar Zazai and Yamin Ahmadzai. Taijul Islam will finish his over with Afsar Zazai taking strike.

Tino Mawoyo is out there for the pitch report. Mawoyo says there has been a lot of rain overnight. He says that the pitch has taken a lot of turn which is more than what happens in Chattogram. Further states that the pitch will take more turn as the day progresses and if you are a left-hander, it will be tough work as the patch of dust will rise up.

Update - 1135 Local - Good news! The pitch inspection is done and play will start at 1150 Local time. Lunch will be taken at 1300 Local with Tea at 1540 and the play will go on till 1740 with an extended half an hour if the overs are not completed.
Update - 11.04 am local (0504 GMT) - We are hearing that the covers are being slowly peeled off and some sunshine has appeared. Fingers crossed for a start soon.
We are getting information that a depression is being formed on the Bay of Bengal and there is forecast for heavy rain for both the days. So a draw cannot be ruled out.

Oh dear. Bad news to begin with. We were supposed to start 20 minutes early but it is raining in Chittagong. However, it is not too heavy at the moment. Hopefully, it is not for very long. Stay tuned for further updates.

Bangladesh would not mind the weather forecast one bit. They have been behind the 8-ball ever since the Afghan-Rahmat partnership in the first innings and not been able to recover. They would love if it rains but then would not want to be over-reliant on the same. Afghanistan would believe that if they get close to 50-60 overs at the home side, they can win this Test. But the longer they bat, the better it will be for the Bangladeshis.

Hola there! Day 4, only Test. Final day probably? Who knows. Afghanistan would believe that 374 is more than enough but after what happened to Australia in 'Stokes'ingley, they would just want to get to 400 to bat Bangladesh out of the game. Having said that, the forecast for the remaining two days is iffy. Should that pave way for an overnight declaration?
... Day 4, Session 1 ...

Going to Day 4, Afghanistan would look to add a few more runs to their lead before declaring and they would be hoping that they finish the game on Day 4 itself. Bangladesh are in a huge spot of bother here and only something special will save them from the blushes. Join us on Sunday, 8th September, 20 minutes early at 0940 Local (0340 GMT) for the start of Day 4. Until then, cheers.

Bangladesh, well, seem to be just going through the motions. They would have wanted their last two wickets to last a bit longer than they did and with the ball, would have wished to get quick wickets. They got 3 quickly but once that massive partnership came, shoulders started to droop. Nothing much was available from the track either which made life difficult for the bowlers.

After bowling out the Bangladesh batters for 205, the hosts did not start all that well losing two wickets in the first over itself. But Ibrahim Zadran and Asghar Afghan stitched a magnificent 108-run stand to give an advantage to the visitors. Following their wickets, Rashid Khan played a brief cameo showing signs of declaration but they let the lower order batsmen have all the fun before bad light stopped play.

Another excellent outing for the visitors here, they have gotten a huge lead of 374 runs and are in the driver's seat at the moment. With two days to go still in the Test match, Afghanistan are likely favorites to upset the hosts here.
Well, bad light followed by sprinkles of rain has called for early Stumps on Day 3.

... Day 3, Session 3 ...

A very mediocre bowling performance from the hosts. They have not been able to trouble the Afghanistan batters much in this session and only Taijul managed to get the sole wicket that fell in this play. The hosts will need to improve their performance if they want to stay alive in this contest. The question is can they find any source of inspiration? Join us after the break to find out.

Ibrahim Zadran and Asghar Afghan started the session solidly. The duo raised their respective fifties and  added 108-run in the process. Asghar Afghan though departed quickly after getting to his half ton but Ibrahim has continued along his merry way. He has looked solid out there and is unbeaten on 82. The hosts have solidified their position in this game and now lead by 293 with enough batting yet to come.
100 runs and just a wicket. This stat is good enough to know who won this session. Afghanistan are running away with it.

We are back for the second session! Bangladesh players make their way out to the middle along with Asghar Afghan and Ibrahim Zadran. Nayeem Hasan will start the new session with the ball for the hosts.
... Day 3, Session 2 ...
Can Bangladesh strike a few more blows and find a way to comeback into this Test or will Afghanistan bat them out of the contest? Join us after the break to find out.

4 bowlers used by Bangladesh in this session. Skipper, Shakib Al Hasan and Nayeem Hasan were the two bowlers to get into the wickets column with 2 and 1 respectively. The other bowlers have bowled well, hardly giving away any freebies but the hosts need wickets to stay alive in this contest as the lead is approaching 200, standing at 193 at the break.

After wrapping up the tail early on in the day, Afghanistan came out to bat with a lead of 137. They though got off to a terrible start losing two wickets in the very first over. Ibrahim Zadran and Hashmatullah Shahidi then fought it out for their 24-run stand. The latter though could not continue. Asghar Afghan then joined Ibrahim out in the middle and the duo ensured there were no further casualities before Lunch adding 28 runs together.
Another fascinating session of Test cricket in this match. Both sides will feel satisfied with their efforts.
